name: Modulo Sum
description: You are given a sequence of numbers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n , and a number m . Check if it is possible to choose a non-empty subsequence a i j such that the sum of numbers in this subsequence is divisible by m .
input_specification: The first line contains two numbers, n and m ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 6 , 2 ≤ m ≤ 10 3 ) — the size of the original sequence and the number such that sum should be divisible by it. The second line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ( 0 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ).
output_specification: In the single line print either " YES " (without the quotes) if there exists the sought subsequence, or " NO " (without the quotes), if such subsequence doesn't exist.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 577B — Modulo Sum [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
